title: Detection of objects supported at closed points
statement:
Let $K$ be a separably closed
field and $X$ a scheme of finite type over $K$. Let
$Q\in D(X_{\Et})$ and assume that $Q_{\bar x}\ne0$ only if $x$
is a closed point of $X$. Then

$$
Q=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad H^i(X_{\Et},Q)=0\text{ for all }
i .
$$

(*Source:* Stacks Project, Tag
[0F1G](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F1G).)

proof.text: If $Q=0$, use the zero complex and its zero K-injective resolution in [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded]. Its complex of global sections is zero, so $H^i(X_{\Et},Q)=0$ for every integer $i$.

source.place: Tag 0F1G, lemma-vanishing-closed-points, first paragraph of proof

proof.text: For the converse suppose $H^i(X_{\Et},Q)=0$ for every integer $i$, and put $F_q=\mathcal H^q(Q)$. For a geometric point $\bar x$ over a nonclosed point, the hypothesis gives $Q_{\bar x}=0$, and [lem-kun-stalks-of-cohomology] gives $(F_q)_{\bar x}=\mathcal H^q(Q_{\bar x})=0$. Thus every $F_q$ is supported at closed points, in the precise sense of [def-kun-support].

Let $\mathcal B$ be the objects $j:U\to X$ of the small etale site whose source scheme $U$ is quasi-compact. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], every object is covered by affine open subschemes; each is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact](iii). Their inclusions and their composites with the given etale object are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1),(2), so they form a covering in [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Thus condition (1) of [lem-kun-0bkz] holds. Each $U\in\mathcal B$ is of finite type over $K$: by [lem-kun-etale-lfp], $j$ is locally of finite presentation and hence locally of finite type. Composing with $X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is locally of finite type, since a finitely generated algebra over a finitely generated algebra is finitely generated (adjoin both finite lists of generators). Since $U$ is quasi-compact, its map to the one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is quasi-compact; [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] now gives finite type. In particular $X\in\mathcal B$ by the original finite-type hypothesis.

Fix $j:U\to X$ in $\mathcal B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] its sheaf restriction $F_q|_U$ is $j^{-1}F_q$. For a geometric point $\bar u$ over $u\in U$, [lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback] and [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition], applied to $j$ and $\bar u$, identify $(F_q|_U)_{\bar u}$ with $(F_q)_{j\bar u}$. Consequently a nonzero stalk can occur only over a point $u$ whose image $x=j(u)$ is closed in $X$, by step 2. Choose affine neighbourhoods of $x$ and $u$ with the latter mapping into the former. The affine inclusions are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1); composing the source inclusion with $j$ and cancelling the target inclusion by clauses (2),(3) shows that the resulting affine morphism is etale. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-residue-field-separable] gives that $\kappa(u)/\kappa(x)$ is finite separable. By [lem-kun-closed-point-field](a), $\kappa(x)/K$ is finite, hence $\kappa(u)/K$ is finite (multiply finite vector-space bases). Apply the same clause to the finite-type $K$-scheme $U$ from step 3: $u$ is closed in $U$. Therefore $F_q|_U$ is supported at closed points of $U$.

Apply [lem-kun-0f1f-vanish] to $U$ and $F_q|_U$ for every $U\in\mathcal B$ and every $q\in\mathbf Z$. The field is still the separably closed field $K$; finite type and closed-point support were checked in steps 3 and 4. This gives $H^p(U_{\Et},F_q)=0$ for every $p>0$. Together with the covering property of step 3 this verifies both hypotheses of [lem-kun-0bkz] for the unbounded object $Q$. It follows that $H^q(X_{\Et},Q)=H^0(X_{\Et},F_q)$ for every $q$, since $X\in\mathcal B$. Here degree-zero sheaf cohomology is ordinary sections: in an injective resolution beginning in degree zero, the kernel of the first differential is the sheaf itself, and taking sections preserves that kernel because kernels of sheaves are computed objectwise. By the assumed vanishing, $\Gamma(X_{\Et},F_q)=0$ for every $q$. No lower bound on $Q$ has been imposed.

Apply [lem-kun-0f1f-gen] to $X$ and $F_q$, using step 2. Its conclusion says that the evaluation morphism in [def-kun-global-generated] is an epimorphism. By step 5 the only global section is the zero section, so every summand of this evaluation sends its generator to zero. The evaluation morphism is therefore the zero morphism. A zero epimorphism onto $F_q$ forces $\mathrm{id}_{F_q}=0$ by cancellation, hence $F_q=0$. This works for each integer $q$.
Every cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^q(Q)=F_q$ vanishes by step 6. The zero-object criterion [lem-kun-d-zero-cohomology] therefore gives $Q=0$, proving the reverse implication and the equivalence.
